answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by requiring every identity to lock a refundable bond before it may trade, like timber stacked across a canyon pass: only one narrow crossing exists and each passage costs a deposit. One honest agent pays once, but an attacker minting a thousand fake identities must fund a thousand bonds, each recorded as permanently as marble — public, hard, and impossible to erase. Any identity caught cheating forfeits its bond to the peers it harmed, so fraud costs more than it can ever earn.
